for_terminal_2.headline_for_any_write_up: G0: on the 2018 development pools every sensitive endpoint has an adjusted one-sided half-width above .001 nats (544/544 rows; smallest 0.00220 adjusted, 0.00141 unadjusted at one-sided 95 percent). A .001-nat confirmation claim is not demonstrable at this sample size for ANY mechanism. A .001 point-estimate screen remains meaningful. This is a property of the evidence base, not of a method.
narrow_the_contribution_statement: The unconditional nullspace feasibility test is verbatim Rassouli and Gunduz Proposition 1; cite, do not derive.
The delta=0 linear-cost problem already has a published LP in that paper, including MSE and error-probability utilities.
SRLIP quantifies over all attribute-subset views simultaneously under a stronger pointwise metric; a multi-view novelty claim will not survive review.
Calmon et al. is quasiconvex not convex, needs the protected attribute at apply time, and already proposes conditioning on a named sub-view.
Conditional Privacy Funnel is an occupied name (Rodriguez-Galvez et al. ITW 2021; de Freitas and Geiger CPFSI, Machine Learning 2025). Use role-constrained stochastic release.
Xu and Strohmer needs the sensitive attribute at inference to select the transport map; rule it out on the contract, not on directness.
Cite and distinguish Zamani et al. arXiv:2211.15525 and arXiv:2601.04815; the latter preempts heterogeneous per-role budgets.
Defensible: the deployment contract plus the nested local/coalition role structure solved as a convex program with a linear cost.
do_not_claim: No fitted-model conditional-information result is a population certificate. Binning the coalition view drops a full log 2 leak to exactly zero in the validated fixture.
No confirmation at .001 on any endpoint from this evidence base.
A supervised residence diagnostic can never support a reserved-task transfer claim.
